RESOLVE App

Source: vignettes/articles/app.Rmd
app.Rmd

Predict a vegetation plot’s EUNIS habitat, altitude, slope, plot area, survey year and location from the species recorded on it, with the released models trained on the European Vegetation Archive’s plots. The models run in your browser: your files are read inside this tab and are not uploaded anywhere. The page downloads the models and the elevation model from Zenodo (models, elevation model), the map from OpenStreetMap and, for a map download, the country boundaries from Eurostat GISCO.

1. Your plots

One row per species record: plot ID, species name (World Flora Online), and optionally cover (%), genus and family. Columns are recognised by name, Darwin Core terms included; change any choice below.
One row per plot: plot ID, latitude and longitude (WGS84), and year and month or a date. Each variable uses the coordinates and date where the tables give them; section 2 names what each is predicted from. A variable the header records on some plots (survey year, coordinates, altitude, slope, plot area) has its gaps fitted on the plots that record it.

2. Models

3. Predictions

      Names are matched exactly against the World Flora Online names the models were trained on; check the spelling and the accepted name of each.

        The models know these species by the name the European Vegetation Archive resolved its records to. Each name is matched through EVA's own records, the synonymy of a taxonomic backbone, or its spelling, named beside it.

          Habitat combines its five seeds by majority vote (agreement is the share of seeds naming the class); numeric variables by their mean and standard deviation across seeds; location by the spherical mean and the median distance of the seeds from it. "Species recognised" is the share of the plot's cover held by species the models know. A terrain-corrected altitude or slope weighs the prediction against the elevation model (GLO-30) at the plot and over the square kilometre around it, by the plot's location uncertainty, the seeds' spread and how many of its species the models know; the elevation model's own values stand beside it.

          Terrain values produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-30 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved.
